parsed.explanation: The operative regime for a visitor contains no documented trans-specific exposure: no trans-specific offence remains in force (Section 164 deleted 2026), no documented police targeting, no facility, custody or border rule aimed at trans travellers, and no documented trans-directed violence — though the violence record is dated (2011) and thin, so absence is not proof of safety. Positive evidence: courts granted trans individuals binding relief and government complied; a registered community organisation operates; police non-targeting was documented. Residual weight: Section 167's unresolved status, documented societal discrimination, ~50% neighbour-tolerance, slow implementation of precedents, and dated official hostility. Sits a step below acceptance-with-protections anchors, above any anchor with universal-exposure measures.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border friction, document mismatch practice, or marker examination recorded for visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented either way; visitor's documents issue from home country and do not engage the domestic recognition route.
entry_documents.interaction: The absence of an administrative recognition process is resident-facing only and does not touch a visitor's passport.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrest, custody-placement or detention practice against trans people appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A 2011 report found police did not target same-sex activity; a former president instructed police not to arrest or harass gay people — dated but directionally positive.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No sodomy statute remains against which police leverage could operate after the 2026 deletion; Section 167's status is unresolved.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access, ward, bathroom or shelter rule affecting trans visitors appears.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No evidence of officials rejecting foreign-issued documents at service points.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No visitor-facing care denial, medication seizure or insurance exclusion appears in the record.
care_services.interaction: No evidence on emergency-care treatment of discovered trans visitors either way.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 167 (conduct between women) remains unresolved after the government declined repeal in 2023; societal discrimination against LGBT people documented in 2011; a 2011 deputy-speaker 'kill' statement is dated official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: President deported an anti-gay pastor (2016) and acknowledged victims deserve protection (2018); employment-act and constitutional-orientation rulings are climate signals.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official signals are mixed but the hostile ones are dated; implementation of court precedents rated 'not satisfactory' in 2024.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific rule touching travelling minors or guardians appears.
minors_guardians.interaction: No age-dependent restriction is recorded in the operative regime.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Societal discrimination documented (2011); no trans-specific violence data after 2011 and no denominator — the violence axis is undocumented, not assessed safe.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2011 report found no reported SOGI-based violence that year — dated, weak evidence of the present.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A functioning community organisation and court access exist, but no documented enforcement response to anti-trans violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Implementation of landmark LGBTQI+ rulings assessed 'not satisfactory so far' (May 2024); governments slow to comply.
remedies_unknowns.protection: High court granted two trans individuals binding marker changes and government issued documents; community organisation registered via court order; constitutional rights to dignity, privacy, expression available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts demonstrably work for trans people in individual cases even where systemic implementation lags.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-B documents routine extended secondary screening and discretionary refusals of entry as a recurring visitor exposure. This dossier documents no border or checkpoint exposure at all — the traveller-facing sphere is empty of documented measures — so it sits above that anchor despite its thinner protection record.

0.65-A shows a visitor incident, functioning court relief and a national equality framework covering gender identity. Here no incident is documented, and the equality machinery is thinner (orientation-based employment law, individual court victories, no administrative recognition). The unimplemented precedents and Section 167 uncertainty place it at or slightly below this anchor's level — 0.68 vs 0.65 is close, with no documented exposure offsetting thinner protections.

0.75-C documents trained border officers, a working tribunal, counsel access and compensation for unlawful detention — protections this dossier cannot show. This jurisdiction has comparable court relief for trans individuals but no documented visitor-facing protective machinery, so it sits a step below, with Section 167's unresolved status and documented societal discrimination holding it in the low Reduced Risk range.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime a visitor encounters is one of absence of exposure rather than presence of protection. Same-sex conduct was decriminalised by litigation and the relevant paragraphs deleted from the statute book in 2026; police historically did not target; courts granted two trans individuals binding recognition and the government complied; a community organisation operates legally. No facility rule, custody rule, border practice, care restriction or documented pattern of trans-directed violence appears in the record. Weighing against this: Section 167's unresolved status, societal discrimination, a tolerance figure near half, official implementation of precedents rated unsatisfactory, and a thin, dated violence record (absence of evidence is not safety). Consequence-if-outed is anchored on working courts that have ruled for trans people, not on any documented hostile mechanism. This places the jurisdiction at the bottom of the Reduced Risk band: materially above any anchor with universal-exposure or targeting features, below anchors with documented functioning visitor protections, and only a step above 0.65 rather than higher because documented acceptance of trans people specifically — as distinct from court victories for individuals — is thin.
